s1.syndrome_frame: Enlarging, painful, purplish mass in the ear canal with granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells
salient_findings: Purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal
Irregular, friable surface with bleeding on minimal contact
Lobulated mass extending into the external acoustic canal and parotid space
Bilateral cervical lymph nodes
Marked vascularity of the mass
key_facts: Purplish lump in left ear canal
Cracking and pus-filled sores at the site
3.5 × 2.5 cm mass in left external ear canal
Incisional biopsy revealed atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation

differentials: Primary cutaneous CD8+ aggressive epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma
per_call: Primary cutaneous CD8+ aggressive epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor with rapid growth and friable surface, consistent with clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells on biopsy, matching disease characteristics

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Marked vascularity on CT angiography and bleeding on minimal contact, suggesting vascular tumor

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral cervical lymph nodes and atypical cells on biopsy, raising suspicion for lymphoproliferative disorder

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor with rapid growth and young patient age, consistent with disease demographics

raw.rationale: The presence of a rapidly enlarging, painful mass with bleeding on minimal contact, along with atypical cells on biopsy, suggests an aggressive malignant tumor. Rhabdomyosarcoma is a common soft tissue sarcoma in children that can present with similar symptoms and has a predilection for the head and neck region, including the ear.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple lesions and systemic symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Rare in children and usually presents with more pronounced vascular symptoms

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, and the biopsy description does not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: More commonly presents with bone pain and systemic symptoms, and the biopsy description does not support this diagnosis
